title: The Stag and the Lion
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A Stag was chased by the hounds, and took refuge in a cave, where he hoped to be safe from his pursuers. Unfortunately the cave contained a Lion, to whom he fell an easy prey. "Unhappy that I am," he cried, "I am saved from the power of the dogs only to fall into the clutches of a Lion." Out of the frying-pan into the fire.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what was chasing the Stag?
According to the passage, where did the Stag take refuge?
According to the passage, what did the Stag hope the cave would provide?
options: A place to rest for the night

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the cave actually contain?
According to the passage, what does the Stag cry out as he is caught?
According to the passage, what phrase is given as the fable's moral?
options: Out of the frying-pan into the fire
A stag in the hand is worth two in the bush

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "pursuers" mean in "safe from his pursuers"?
Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: Escaping one danger can lead straight into a worse one
Caves are never a safe place to hide from hounds
Lions are always more dangerous than hounds
It is better to face hounds than to hide at all

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what word describes what the Stag did upon reaching the cave?
According to the passage, what does the Stag say he is saved from, only to fall into something worse?
According to the passage, what does the Stag say he falls into?
As the passage uses it, what does "refuge" mean in "took refuge in a cave"?
options: A place of shelter or safety

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why is the Stag's fate especially bitter?
options: The very place he chose for safety turns out to hold a greater danger than the one he was fleeing
He was caught by the hounds before he even reached the cave
The Lion had been chasing him the whole time as well
He could have easily defeated the Lion if he had tried

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A Stag fleeing hounds hides in a cave, only to be caught by a Lion waiting inside
A Stag outruns both the hounds and a Lion to reach safety
A Lion protects a Stag from a pack of hounds
A Stag and a Lion share a cave peacefully to avoid the hounds
